name: Illinois

benefitCategories.medical: All reasonable and necessary treatment; no fee schedule caps (one of few states)
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages; no statutory max rate cap; max 401 weeks or until MMI
benefitCategories.permanentPartial: Schedule (specific loss): 60% of wages × weeks per body part; Non-schedule: based on wage differential
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages for life plus cost-of-living adjustments
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 66 2/3% of wages to dependents for 25 years or until remarriage/child majority; $8,000 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: Application for Adjustment of Claim filed with IWCC

appealLevels.name: Arbitrator Hearing
appealLevels.deadline: 3 years from injury (2 years if no comp paid)

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: IWCC adjudication; petitions for penalties; fraud prosecution
workersCompensation.penalties: 50% penalty for unreasonable delay/denial; attorney fees; penalties under § 19(k) and 19(l)

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Illinois has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: Illinois Medicaid
programs.administeringBody: IL Dept. of Healthcare and Family Services
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Illinois expanded Medicaid under ACA
programs.wcInteraction: WC primary for work injuries; Medicaid covers non-work care

programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance
programs.wcInteraction: WC income counted in eligibility determination

continuityGaps: Gap between WC and SSDI approval
terminationRisks: Settlement without consideration of future needs

statutes.name: Illinois Human Rights Act
statutes.protections: Disability discrimination; broader than some states; includes handicap unrelated to ability

statutes.name: Victims' Economic Security and Safety Act (VESSA)

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing charges, testifying, or assisting in proceedings

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation; pregnancy accommodations mandatory (Pregnancy Fairness amendments)
accommodationObligations.process: Interactive process; broader pregnancy accommodations than federal

enablingStatutes.disability: No state TDI; 305 ILCS 5 (Public Aid Code)

laborStandards.authority: Wage Payment and Collection Act; minimum wage; child labor

occupationalSafety.authority: Illinois is not a state plan state for private sector; OSHA covers private; state covers state/local public employees

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 3 years from injury (2 years if no compensation paid); 45 days notice to employer recommended
filingDeadlines.ihrcHearing: 90 days after IDHR finding; or request early dismissal for court

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; chain of causation
evidentiaryStandards.idhr: Substantial evidence for finding; preponderance at IHRC
evidentiaryStandards.iwcc: Commission decision is prima facie correct on review

judicialReview.wc: Arbitrator → IWCC Commission → Circuit Court → Appellate Court → Supreme Court
judicialReview.civilRights: IDHR → IHRC (or elect circuit court after filing) → Appellate Court
judicialReview.directFiling: May request early dismissal from IDHR to proceed directly to circuit court

specialConsiderations.noFeeSchedule: Illinois is one of few states without a medical fee schedule; healthcare costs higher but access typically better
specialConsiderations.strongUnionPresence: Labor-friendly state; union contracts may enhance benefits
specialConsiderations.chicagoOrdinances: Chicago has additional human rights ordinances with local enforcement
